# Review round 1

Branch docs/issue-316-flow-prompt-audit. Findings below are copied verbatim from each reviewer subagent's final report: the section headings (which carry the severity) and every finding row or line that names tier-gate.sh, block-unchecked-merge.sh, block-destructive.sh, command-parse.sh, or their test files. Lines that do not name those files are omitted.

## Code review (HEAD 8d2b41ce)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-ae375a9fbdad15857.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-29T19:09:02.259Z

**Recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES.** I reviewed the branch at HEAD `8d2b41ce08f5df62c55b97b68e1ea09de4347df0` against `main`. There is one P1: the new tier hook does not ask before a release or tag push when the command starts with `if`, `!`, `{`, `for … do` or `until`. Merges in those forms are still refused, but only because a separate hook catches them.
## Code Review Findings
### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
| **F1 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:257-283`**<br>`_tg_command_word` skips only `VAR=value` assignments and the listed wrappers. A shell keyword or `{` in front of the command becomes the command word, so the action is never classified. I ran the hook (in a scratch repository) on each of these, and each exited 0 with no output, meaning no prompt and no trail entry: `if gh release create v1 --notes x; then echo ok; fi`, `{ git push origin --tags; }`, `! git push origin v1:refs/tags/v1`, `for r in a; do gh release create v1; done`, `make && { gh release create v1; }`, and `if gh pr merge 1; then …`, `until gh pr merge 1; do …`. These are normal commands an agent writes, not the "deliberate evasion" the header excludes (lines 129-133). Nothing else covers the release side: `block-unchecked-merge.sh` also allowed all four release and tag-push forms. For merge, `block-unchecked-merge.sh` refuses `!`, `{` and `do` (exit 2), so merge is covered only by that hook. This matters more now because `release.md` and `merge.md` removed their AskUserQuestion confirmation and rely on this hook for Tier 3. The push, prCreate and issueCreate journal entries are skipped in the same forms. `tests/e2e-tier-gate.test.sh` has no case that starts with a keyword or `{`. _(HIGH)_ | Before the wrapper loop, skip a leading `!`, `{`, `(`, `if`, `then`, `elif`, `else`, `while`, `until`, `do` and `time -p`, or have the parser split segments at `{`, `then` and `do`. Add each probe above to `e2e-tier-gate.test.sh` as a case that must ask. |
### P2 — Should Fix
| **F2 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:637-648`**<br>The same action gets two answers. `gh api repos/o/r/releases/1 -X PATCH -f draft=false` asks, but `gh release edit v1 --draft=false` (publishing a draft release) is allowed silently. Both ran through the hook. _(HIGH)_ | Classify `release edit` with `--draft=false` (and `--prerelease=false`, `--tag`) as `release` in `_tg_gh`, or name the exclusion in the header. |
### P3 — Consider
### Summary
  - `tier-gate.sh`, `flow-judge.sh`, `flow-goal-judge-run.sh`
  - `tier-gate.sh`: 1 (`lib/command-parse.sh`, which it reuses).
- **Ran:** the tier-gate probes (F1, F2), the commit repro (F3), and the merge-hook cross-check. The probe files are in `<scratch>` (`probe.sh`, `c1.txt`, `c2.txt`, `c3.txt`).

## Security review (HEAD 8d2b41ce)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-a53dc46f82abd23b3.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-29T19:10:10.772Z

I found 5 P1, 6 P2 and 3 P3 security issues on this branch, and my decision is **REQUEST_CHANGES**. The main problem is that `tier-gate.sh` lets a release or a tag push through without asking when the command is written in ordinary forms like an `if` block or a `for` loop. That hook is now the only confirmation for releases.
**How the findings were checked.** Each hook result came from feeding a PreToolUse payload to the hook in a scratch repo; the payloads are in `<scratch>`. The git behaviour was confirmed by pushing to a local bare remote (git 2.55.0). I ran the named suite `tests/run.sh e2e-tier-gate.test.sh`: 729 pass, 0 fail, with every bypass below still open.
**Merge versus release.** `block-unchecked-merge.sh` (not changed on this branch) refuses any `gh pr merge` that is not in its one accepted form, and any GraphQL call that mentions merge. So most of the merge bypasses are caught there; the one that is not is the backslash case (SEC-2). Releases and tag pushes have no second hook, and `release.md` no longer asks the user before publishing.
## Security Review Findings
### P1 — Critical Security Issues (Blocks Merge)
| **SEC-1 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:257`**<br>`_tg_command_word` skips only `VAR=value` and the wrapper list. When a shell keyword comes first, the keyword is read as the program and nothing matches. These all ran with no prompt: `if true; then gh release create v9; fi`, the same with `elif` and `else`, `{ git push --tags; }`, `! git push --tags`, `for t in v1; do git push origin v1; done`, `select ... do`, `function f { gh release create v9; }`, `coproc gh release create v9`. These are normal ways to write shell, not deliberate evasion, so they contradict the header's claim (lines 129–139) that the hook reads commands written in good faith. `gh pr merge` in the same forms is refused by `block-unchecked-merge.sh:262`, but release and tag push have no backstop. _(HIGH)_ | Skip the keywords `if then elif else do while until for select case { } ! [[ function coproc` (and `name()` definitions) before finding the command word. Add these as T5 rows for release and push. |
| **SEC-2 · security/injection · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:233`**<br>`_tg_prog` removes only a leading backslash, and the shared tokenizer keeps backslashes inside a word. Bash removes them before running, so `g\h pr merge 1`, `gh pr mer\ge 1`, `gh p\r merge 1`, `gh rel\ease create v9` and `git pu\sh --tags` all ran. Both this hook and `block-unchecked-merge.sh` allowed all three merge spellings. This is a merge **and** release bypass with nothing else catching it. The header's exclusion covers "a quote inside the word", not backslashes. _(HIGH)_ | Remove backslashes from each token before matching. Or treat any token in the command-word or subcommand position that contains `\` as unreadable and ask. Apply the same fix in `block-unchecked-merge.sh`. |
| **SEC-3 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:402`**<br>`git push` options are matched only as exact strings. Git accepts any unique prefix of a long option and bundled short options. Each of these pushed or deleted tags on a real remote and was allowed as a branch push: `--tag`, `--mirr`, `--follow-tag`, `--del v1`, `-qd origin v1`. `block-force-push.sh` catches only the bundles that contain `-f`. _(HIGH)_ | Match long options by unique prefix (`--t*`, `--mi*`, `--fo*`, `--de*`). Treat any short-option bundle containing `d` as `--delete`. |
| **SEC-4 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:433`**<br>A name that resolves to neither a tag nor a branch is treated as a branch push unless the repository could not be found (`TG_UNRES=1`). Line 380 also returns `unknown` for any `*`. Three cases follow, all verified:<br>1. `git push origin tags/v1` (git expands it to the tag) and `git push origin 'refs/*:refs/*'` push tags with no prompt.<br>2. `git tag v7.0.0 && git push origin v7.0.0` in one call: the tag does not exist yet when the hook runs, so the push is only journaled as `tiers.push`.<br>3. The next `gh release create v7.0.0 --verify-tag` is then also only journaled (lines 747–754), because the tag is now on the remote.<br>Together that is a full release with no prompt, using the obvious spelling. _(HIGH)_ | Ask whenever a refspec source is `unknown` or contains a glob, whatever `TG_UNRES` says. Do not let the `--verify-tag` journaling cover a tag that was pushed while journaled at the push tier, or drop that exemption. |
| **SEC-5 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:637`**<br>The `gh` subcommand table has no `release edit` or `release delete`. `gh release edit v1 --draft=false` publishes a release, and `gh release delete v1 --cleanup-tag` deletes a tag. Both were allowed, although their REST equivalents are gated as release (PATCH `releases/{id}` at line 552, DELETE `git/refs/tags` at line 540). _(HIGH)_ | Map `release edit` and `release delete` (and `release upload` if publishing assets counts as releasing) to `release`. |
### P2 — Security Concerns
| **SEC-6 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:264`**<br>The wrapper list is fixed. These were allowed: `caffeinate`, `stdbuf -o0`, `setsid`, `watch -n1`, `find … -exec`, `parallel`, `script -q /dev/null`, and `builtin command` (the brief specifically lists `command` wrappers). Each was tested with `gh release create` or `git push --tags`. _(HIGH)_ | Add these to the wrapper list, with their value-taking options. Or ask when `gh` or `git push` appears as a word anywhere after a word that is not one of the program's own arguments. |
| **SEC-7 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:503`**<br>The GraphQL mutation list does not include `createRef`, `updateRef` or `deleteRef`. `createRef` with `name:"refs/tags/v9"` was allowed, although its REST equivalent (POST `git/refs` with `refs/tags/`) is gated at line 577. The header excludes unlisted mutations by design, but these are the GraphQL versions of an action already gated. (`enqueuePullRequest` is denied by `block-unchecked-merge.sh`.) _(HIGH)_ | Add `createRef`, `updateRef` and `deleteRef` and route them as release. Ask for `updateRef`/`deleteRef` too, since the ref name cannot be read from them. |
| **SEC-8 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:336`**<br>Of the `-c` settings, only `push.followTags` is read. `git -c remote.origin.mirror=true push origin` pushes every tag and was allowed. `-c remote.<name>.push=refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` and repository config of `remote.*.mirror` / `remote.*.push` are not checked either. _(HIGH)_ | Treat any `-c remote.*.mirror` or `-c remote.*.push` as a possible tag push. Read `remote.<name>.mirror` and `push` from config the same way `push.followTags` is read. |
| **SEC-11 · security/test-gap · `plugins/flow/tests/e2e-tier-gate.test.sh:260`**<br>The T5 and T13 rows contain none of the spellings in SEC-1 to SEC-8. The suite passed 729/0 with all of them open, so nothing pins the guarantee that `merge.md` and `release.md` now rely on. _(HIGH)_ | Add must-ask rows for every spelling above, and run each fix's mutant to show its row fails without it. |
### P3 — Security Improvements
| **SEC-13 · security/authz · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:709`**<br>Without `-R`, the `--verify-tag` lookup checks `origin`. `gh` may target a different repository (`GH_REPO=` prefix, or `gh repo set-default`). So the journaled exemption can be granted because the tag exists in one repository while the release is created in another. _(MEDIUM)_ | Read a `GH_REPO=` assignment prefix. Ask when no `-R` is given and gh's default repository is not `origin`. |

## Error-handling review (HEAD 8d2b41ce)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-a2096df289b801d03.jsonl` (final assistant message)

## Error Handling Inspection
Checked against HEAD 8d2b41ce on `docs/issue-316-flow-prompt-audit`, diff `main...HEAD`. Four findings were reproduced in a scratch directory: ERR-2, ERR-3, ERR-8, and the jq check behind a non-finding. The tier-gate probe ran 32 edge-case commands through `tier-gate.sh` under `/bin/bash` 3.2.57; every one exited 0 and the merge, release and tag cases all returned `ask`. Everything else comes from reading the code path. I did not run the LSP step (the changed code is shell, Python and markdown fences) and did not run any `tests/run.sh` suite.
### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
### P2 — Should Fix
### P3 — Consider
| **ERR-8 · error-handling · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:720-725`**<br>`kill "$w"` on the watchdog job has no suppressed `wait`. Under bash 3.2, every `gh release create … --verify-tag` call prints `line 706: <pid> Terminated: 15 ( sleep …` to the hook's stderr; observed in the probe. The comment at 722-724 says that report is suppressed, but only the git job's is. _(HIGH)_ | `{ kill "$w"; wait "$w"; } 2>/dev/null`. |
| **ERR-9 · silent-failure · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:193`**<br>`… jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' … \|\| COMMAND=""` treats a payload jq cannot parse the same as an empty command: exit 0, no stderr line, and the merge/release text check never runs. The header's decision table covers jq being missing, not jq failing. _(MEDIUM)_ | `\|\| _tg_undecidable "$INPUT" "the hook payload could not be parsed"`, matching the jq-missing path. |
### Summary
- Files inspected: 16. Priority list: tier-gate.sh, flow-goal-evaluator.sh, flow-judge.sh, flow-goal-judge-run.sh, journal-append.sh, journal-record.sh, `_flow_release_versions.py`, flow-release-versions.sh, `_flow_watch_create.py`, flow-watch-create.sh, flow-skill-manifests.sh, flow-pr-feedback.sh, flow-trigger-schema-check.sh, and the fences in release.md, merge.md and watch.md. Also read where they connect: the `--verdict-input` change in `_journal_atomic.py` and `_flow_evidence_bundle.py`, `start.md` step 6, the trigger-policy skill's Step 1, and hooks.json.
- Checked and not reported: jq accepts invalid UTF-8 in `--arg` (tested, rc=0). `_tg_actions` exiting non-zero is handled as "cannot decide". The evaluator's handling of an empty or out-of-enum judge reply blocks the turn as documented. merge.md's move from AskUserQuestion to the tier-gate prompt depends on Claude Code showing a hook `ask` in bypassPermissions mode; I could not check that from here.
